name: אִי־כָבוֹד
gloss: no glory; or where is glory?
summary: The son of Phinehas, born as his mother died on hearing that the ark of God was taken and that Eli and Phinehas were dead. She named him from the disaster: “glory has gone into exile from Israel”, for the ark was taken (1Sa 4:21–22). The name is אִי, “not” (as in Job 22:30, אִי־נָקִי “one not innocent”) or perhaps “where?”, with כָּבוֹד, “glory”: the glory that was Israel's, Yahweh's presence with the ark, is gone. He is named again as the brother of Ahitub, uncle of Ahijah the priest (1Sa 14:3, spelled אִיכָבוֹד).

evidence.note: “She called the boy אִי־כָבוֹד, saying, Glory has gone into exile (גָּלָה כָבוֹד) from Israel, because the ark of God was taken, and because of her father-in-law and her husband.”
“Glory has gone into exile from Israel, for the ark of God is taken.”
His birth as his mother died.
“Ahijah son of Ahitub, the brother of אִיכָבוֹד, son of Phinehas, son of Eli.”
אִי as a negative: אִי־נָקִי, “the not-innocent”.
Of the same day: “he gave his strength into captivity and his splendour into the hand of the enemy”.

note: BDB files the name under אי (a.cw.ab); the second word's tokens at 1Sa 4:21 are also keyed k.af.af. Whether אִי here is the negative (Job 22:30; Phoenician ʾy) or the interrogative “where?” is open (see the note in eyn.json); the gloss gives both. The scripture's own explanation (1Sa 4:21–22) rests on כָּבוֹד either way.
